extracted.intended_audience: credit card issuers, compliance officers, legal counsel, and regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Federal rulemaking and official interpretive guidance amending Regulation Z (12 CFR 1026) governing credit card penalty fees—especially late fees—including safe-harbor amounts, cost-analysis requirements, definitions of issuer size, disclosure and sample-form requirements, and related procedural obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: TILA §149 'reasonable and proportional' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of any penalty fee with respect to a credit card account must be 'reasonable and proportional' to the omission or violation to which the fee relates (TILA section 149).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In implementing this standard, the Board/CFPB must consider: (1) the cost incurred by the creditor from an omission or violation; (2) the deterrence of omissions or violations by the cardholder; (3) the conduct of the cardholder; and (4) other factors deemed necessary or appropriate. The CFPB frames safe harbors and cost-analysis provisions as mechanisms to ensure fees satisfy this statutory standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-analysis requirement (§1026.52(b)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A card issuer that does not use the safe-harbor provision must determine that the dollar amount of a penalty fee 'represents a reasonable proportion of the total costs incurred by the issuer for that type of violation' through a cost analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cost-analysis approach requires issuers to calculate costs attributable to the violation and set fees proportional to those costs. The CFPB explicitly clarifies (comment 52(b)(1)(i)-2.i) that costs do not include collection costs incurred after an account is charged off pursuant to loan loss provisions. CFPB found little evidence issuers use the cost-analysis path in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe-harbor alternative (§1026.52(b)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: As an alternative to cost analysis, a card issuer may comply with specified safe-harbor dollar amounts set in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii) to satisfy the 'reasonable and proportional' requirement for penalty fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers choosing the safe harbor need not do a detailed cost analysis. However, compliance with the safe harbor does not permit imposition of fees that are inconsistent with §1026.52(b)(2) prohibitions (e.g., fees that exceed the dollar amount associated with the violation or multiple fees for one event). The final rule revises safe-harbor amounts for different issuer sizes and fee types (see separate entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Late-fee safe-harbor for Larger Card Issuers ($8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For card issuers that together with their affiliates have one million or more open credit card accounts ('Larger Card Issuers'), the final rule adopts a late-fee safe-harbor dollar amount of $8 and repeals the prior higher safe-harbor thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For these Larger Card Issuers, CFPB also eliminates the higher safe-harbor dollar amount that previously applied to repeat violations within the same billing cycle or the next six billing cycles, and provides that annual CPI-based adjustments in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(D) will not apply to the $8 amount. The CFPB explains this is to ensure late fees are consistent with TILA's requirement that such fees be reasonable and proportional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe-harbor amounts for Smaller Card Issuers and other penalty fees ($32/$43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the rule's annual adjustments, the safe-harbor threshold amounts in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(A) and (B) are revised to $32 generally and $43 for each subsequent violation occurring in the same billing cycle or the next six billing cycles; these revised amounts apply to penalty fees other than late fees for all card issuers and to late fees imposed by Smaller Card Issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule does not adopt the $8 late-fee safe harbor for Smaller Card Issuers (those with fewer than one million open accounts); instead Smaller Card Issuers remain subject to the revised $32/$43 safe-harbor amounts (which continue to be subject to annual CPI adjustments). CFPB notes that many smaller issuers already charge well below the safe harbor amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on fees that exceed dollar amount associated with violation (§1026.52(b)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1026.52(b)(2)(i) prohibits card issuers from imposing penalty fees that exceed the dollar amount associated with the violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition operates independently of the safe harbor and cost-analysis approaches; an issuer may not use a safe harbor or cost analysis to justify a fee that is otherwise prohibited (example in text: if §1026.52(b)(2)(i) prohibits a late fee exceeding $7, §1026.52(b)(1)(ii) cannot be used to impose a larger fee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on multiple fees for a single event (§1026.52(b)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1026.52(b)(2)(ii) prohibits imposing multiple penalty fees based on a single event or transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers may not layer fees for the same underlying omission/transaction; the rule and commentary emphasize that (b)(1) safe harbors do not authorize conduct barred by (b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Smaller Card Issuer' (§1026.52(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule defines 'Smaller Card Issuer' to mean a card issuer that together with its affiliates had fewer than one million open credit card accounts for the entire preceding calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This size-based definition determines whether an issuer is subject to the $8 late-fee safe harbor (Larger Card Issuers) or the revised $32/$43 safe harbors (Smaller Card Issuers). The definition relies on the open-account concept from §1026.58(b)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'open credit card account' (§1026.58(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'open credit card account' is defined as a credit card account under an open-end (not home-secured) consumer credit plan where (1) the cardholder can obtain extensions of credit on the account; or (2) there is an outstanding balance on the account that has not been charged off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is used to count accounts for the Smaller/Larger Card Issuer size determination and to determine applicability of certain provisions of subpart G and the safe harbors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification excluding post-charge-off collection costs from cost analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule amends comment 52(b)(1)(i)-2.i to state explicitly that costs for purposes of the cost-analysis provisions do not include any collection costs incurred after an account is charged off pursuant to loan loss provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarification applies to all issuers that use the cost-analysis provisions to determine penalty fee amounts and was adopted to limit the costs that may be recovered via penalty fees to those reasonably related to the violation before charge-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic statement disclosure requirements (§1026.7; 7(b)(11) Due Date; Late Payment Costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation Z provisions governing periodic statements require specific disclosures related to new balance, due date, late payment, and minimum payment information for open-end (not home-secured) plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule amends comment 7(b)(11)-4 and related sample forms to revise examples of late fee amounts and illustrate how the $8 safe harbor would appear in periodic statement examples. Sample forms (Appendix G) reflect the adopted safe-harbor amounts where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and tabular format requirement for applications/solicitations (§1026.60(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Credit and charge card applications and solicitations must provide disclosures in the required form, including a tabular format for certain disclosures under §1026.60(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule amends comment 60(a)(2)-5.ii and sample forms to update examples so they are consistent with the adopted safe-harbor amounts. CFPB's guidance clarifies how safe-harbor limits should be reflected in marketing and application disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix G model/sample forms updates (e.g., G-18 series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix G model forms and clauses (e.g., G-18(A), G-18(B), G-18(D), G-18(F), G-18(G)) must be revised to reflect the safe-harbor late-fee amounts and to illustrate appropriate disclosures such as 'Late Fee Warning' and 'Fees.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB discusses how sample forms should present late-fee warnings and the fees actually charged in a billing cycle. For example, discussion notes that a 15-day courtesy-period disclosure (if adopted) would be appropriate for the 'Late Fee Warning' but not for the example of an assessed fee under 'Fees.' The final rule revises examples to be consistent with the $8 safe harbor for Larger Card Issuers and $32/$43 for other contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change-in-terms notice when issuer size changes (§1026.9 implications)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Larger Card Issuer becomes a Smaller Card Issuer, the issuer must provide consumers a change-in-terms notice at least 45 days prior to imposing higher late-fee amounts under the safe harbor; if a Smaller Card Issuer becomes a Larger Card Issuer, the issuer is not required to provide notice prior to imposing lower late-fee amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule interaction is consistent with §1026.9(c)(2)(i)(A) and (c)(2)(v)(A). The notice timing aims to protect consumers when an issuer increases permissible late fees due to a size-category change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual CPI adjustments to safe-harbor dollar amounts (§1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(D))
rubrics_metrics.description: Safe-harbor dollar amounts in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii) are subject to annual adjustments to reflect changes in the Consumer Price Index (CFPB uses CPI-W for adjustments), with changes of $1 or more producing an adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule applies these annual adjustments to the revised safe-harbor amounts (e.g., the $32/$43 amounts) but explicitly provides that the $8 late-fee safe-harbor for Larger Card Issuers will not be adjusted annually under §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(D). CFPB discusses index choice and historical relationships between costs and CPI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed/solicited changes (not adopted in final rule): 25% cap, 15-day courtesy period, and automatic-payment/notification conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2023 proposal solicited comments on several potential additional limits and conditions, including: (a) limiting late fees to 25 percent of the required payment (proposal to amend §1026.52(b)(2)(i)(A)); (b) prohibiting late fees imposed within 15 calendar days after the payment due date (a 15-day courtesy period); and (c) as a condition of using the safe harbor, requiring issuers to offer automatic payment options or provide payment-due-date notifications within a specified number of days prior to the due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These were proposals the CFPB solicited comment on; the final rule describes the proposals and comments received but did not adopt several of these changes for all issuers. CFPB explains rationale, potential impacts, and which proposals were accepted, modified, or rejected in the final rule discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship and consistency requirement between (b)(1) and (b)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1026.52(b)(1) (cost-analysis or safe-harbor approaches) does not permit a card issuer to impose a fee that is inconsistent with the prohibitions in §1026.52(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB provides the example that (b)(1)(ii) cannot be used to impose a late fee higher than the dollar amount that (b)(2)(i) prohibits. This preserves (b)(2) as a baseline limit on permissible fee structure regardless of safe-harbor use.
